Hi Karthik / Vanessa,

Thanks for moving quickly on the MSA + Order Form. Before we proceed to signature, our InfoSec and procurement teams have a couple of asks so we can close internal approval:

- Can you confirm the pen-test window and level of access we should expect for a scoped test? (on-prem equivalent / staging only?)
- We need clarity on the SOC 2 evidence cadence (sampled artifacts vs. continuous logs) and what you can reasonably deliver on a monthly vs. quarterly basis.
- On audit rights: will Redwood accept a timeboxed inspection window and sampling carve-outs? Procurement is pushing for a 90-day notice to schedule with narrow sampling bands.

Subject: Re: Audit rights language / SOC2 evidence cadence

Claire — thanks for the clear asks. High-level proposal below and I've attached a short redline summary to make legal review faster.

Proposal (summary):
- Pen-test window: 2-week scheduled window in staging; tests run against ephemeral credentials and isolated test accounts. Technical contacts + on-call response available during the window.
- SOC 2 evidence: we propose monthly delivery of a limited artifact set (control mappings, exception logs, change history) and quarterly full artifact bundles for auditors. We can also offer a live read-only streaming session for specific logs if required.
- Audit rights: Redwood cannot grant unlimited live inspection. Proposed contract language: timeboxed inspection windows (max 14 days notice for routine sampling; 90 days for full inspections), bounded sampling (we will mutually agree scope and number of sample records), and an obligation to coordinate any production impact.

Attached: karthik_redline_summary.pdf (pdf) — short bullets against MSA + Order Form.

Next steps: Laura (legal) — can you review the attached redline summary and propose specific clause text? Vanessa — can you propose an operational runbook (evidence checklist + contact list) we can attach or reference in the Order Form?

Happy to jump on a 30-minute call this week to align.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of GTM Legal Operations, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Audit rights language / SOC2 evidence cadence

Thanks — I reviewed Karthik's summary and drafted a set of tracked changes for the MSA Order Form. High level legal positions:

1) Inspection rights must be bounded and reciprocal where possible. We cannot accept language that allows unlimited on-site or live production access. Recommend: define "Inspection Period" (max 14 calendar days) and require mutual written scope sign-off 10 business days prior to start.

2) Pen-test language: agree to permit third-party pen-tests in staging with vendor-approved scope. Require written attestation of no lateral movement to production and a maximum of 48 hours to remediate any critical issues discovered (or agreed mitigation plan).

3) Evidence delivery: define artifact sets by name (SOC2: control matrix, exception log, change-history snapshots). For audit requests outside the normal cadence, require a written estimate of effort and reasonable cost recovery if additional ad-hoc collection is requested.

I've attached msaredline_track_changes.docx with clause-level edits and rationale comments. I tried to preserve MedAlign's ability to audit while protecting our operational constraints.

Attachments: msaredline_track_changes.docx (Word)

Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Audit rights language / SOC2 evidence cadence

Looping in the practical ops plan — this is what we do day-to-day and what I recommend we commit to in the Order Form appendix (Assurance Runbook).

Operational proposal (Assurance Runbook summary):
- Monthly: delivery of the Assurance Matrix (attachment) that maps SOC 2 controls to artifacts we can export; includes timestamps and owner.
- Quarterly: full artifact bundle for auditors (logs, config snapshots, change-history, access reviews) delivered as read-only exports via secure Drive link.
- Pen-test: 14-day notice to schedule; testing strictly in our staging environment. We provide ephemeral credentials and a test feature flag to disable harmful actions. On-call engineer assigned during the two-week window.
- Emergency sampling: if MedAlign identifies a high-severity event, we will prioritize a targeted evidence pull within 5 business days; for anything beyond standard scope, we will provide an estimated hours/cost and scheduling window.

Action items I propose we include in the Order Form appendix:
1) Assurance contact list + escalation ladder (we'll provide names & mobile numbers).
2) Evidence export templates (artifact list + format).
3) Standard SLAs for turnaround on ad-hoc evidence requests (5 biz days for urgent, 20 biz days for non-urgent).

Attached: assurance_matrix.xlsx (Excel) — draft artifact matrix.

Claire — if that aligns with your internal reviewers, I can convert this into an appendix to be referenced from the Order Form (reduces legal friction).

Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
